about: ARKBOARD Process: the definition and method for every metric and model, and the FV conversion chart for each board.

entries.short: FV is a grade on the 20-80 scale of what a prospect becomes at his peak, set as the mean outcome of past players with the same profile.
body: 50 is an average regular, 60 is a plus player, 70 is a star and 80 is generational. Tiers are every 5 points and grades move in steps of 1.
Each board has its own outcome and rarity ladder. There is no shared FV scale across sports.
The headline is the mean of the tier odds, busts and stars included, so it sits below the best case.
The grade is absolute talent, read from a fixed map fit on pooled history, not a rank within a class or a board.
A strong class gets more high grades. Age and the drivers that pass held out move the grade.
entries.where: Every prospect board: CFB, CBB, hockey prospects, soccer prospects, tennis prospects; recruit tabs; MLB boards

entries.short: The outcome ladder is the realized result each FV tier stands for, set by how rare it is on each board.
body: CFB: the NFL career (All-Pro, Pro Bowl, seasons as a starter), from the 2012-18 drafts.
CBB: peak NBA XPM, as rare as the matching NBA role (7+ All-NBA teams = 80), for careers ending 2008-16.
Hockey: peak NHL pWAR (best 3 of the first 7 seasons), by rarity in a draft class, 2008-19 classes.
Soccer: peak GAR at ages 22-26, by rarity in a birth year and position group, for players who were 22 in 2013-21.
Tennis: peak ranking points above No. 200 at ages 22-28, by rarity in a birth year on each tour, births 1979-97.
The ATP fit also trains on births after 1997, with partial careers imputed to a final outcome.
entries.where: fv model tab on each prospect page; FV conversion charts below

entries.short: Above each board's knot K the headline runs in a straight line to 80 at T, so an 80 comes about once every 5 seasons.
body: The mean of a capped outcome can never reach 80. The stretch makes 80 reachable, but rare.
K is the mean that about 3 players a season reach, and T is the level one player reaches about every 5 seasons (exponential tail, held out).
The order of players doesn't change. The exact mean (fvx) stays in the tooltips, and above K the headline reads higher than the realized means.
entries.where: Headline FV on every prospect board (data/fv_scale.json)

entries.short: Each player's odds of reaching every outcome tier, and his 10th to 90th percentile outcome.
body: CFB and CBB use a location-scale ordered probit of the realized outcome on the grade, with cut points at 30, 35 ... 70.
A spread term is kept only if it improves held-out RPS (CFB: early season ×2.1, walk-on, consensus, underclassman).
Held out, CFB RPS is .0398 compared to .0408 with one spread, and CBB is .0767. Hockey, soccer and tennis use logistic odds for each tier.
The odds are shown in the player dropdown only. The main boards show the single headline.

entries.term: Tier chances (NBA%, NHL%, Top%, Reg%, Star%)
entries.short: The chance a player reaches a set outcome tier.
body: CBB NBA% is the chance he plays in the NBA, the first rung of the FV model.
Hockey NHL% is the chance of 40+ (top 45 of a class), and Reg% is 50+ (an NHL regular, top 20 of a class).
Soccer Top% is 40+ (a top-flight regular, top 250 of a birth year at the position), Reg% is 50+ (top 90) and Star% is 60+ (top 20).
entries.where: Board columns: CBB, hockey prospects, soccer prospects

entries.short: A + marks a player whose odds of becoming a star beat those of a player 2.5 FV higher, because of his age.
body: The rule: + when P(60+ | FV, age) >= P(60+ | FV + 2.5). Age is the only upside signal that passed held out.
Held out, soccer is t = 5.0 / 4.1 at 55+ / 60+, tennis ATP t = 4.3 / 3.3 and WTA 3.9 / 3.1. About 6% of tennis prospects and 30% of the soccer top 2000 get one.
The CFB version failed held out (t = -.71 / -.34) and was removed. No signal passed in CBB or hockey.
entries.where: Soccer prospects and tennis prospects boards

entries.short: A player with only a birth year gets the mean birth day for his class, instead of Oct 15.
body: k = first D-I season - birth year - (class - 1).
Mean day of the year by k, from 16,744 day-precise careers: k 19 Apr 30, k 20 Jul 24, k 21+ Aug 22.
Held out on 942 board players who entered in 2023 or later,
mean absolute age error goes from .347 yr (Oct 15) and .258 (Jul 1) to .237 (t = 15.6 and 5.8).
FIBA youth rosters on file add a day-precise date when the birth year agrees with Barttorvik's.
1,401 of 1,427 checked dates were within 3 days.

entries.short: A player who isn't on the source board gets a provisional grade, which starts at the 20 floor and takes every driver available for him.
body: He is ranked in FV order with a prov tag. CBB uses a ridge on height, weight, class, age, recruit rank and the team's top-8 FV (R² .77).
Hockey grades OHL, WHL, QMJHL, AHL and Liiga draft-eligibles from Tankathon on NHLe, age, weight and position.
Soccer gives academy-only and youth-international players their own provisional line.
CFB grades ESPN roster backups and carried-over players up from the 20 floor.

entries.short: The scorecard checks each board held out: the FV band a player was given against what he became.
body: For each band it shows the mean FV given and the mean reached (90% CI), and the predicted 40+, 50+ and 60+ odds against the realized share.
Slopes: CFB .99, CBB .97, soccer 1.01, tennis ATP .99 and WTA .97. Hockey is calibrated.
Where it runs hot: WTA 45-64 by 2.5-4.8, and CFB 40+ odds by 6-8 points at FV 40-49.
entries.where: fv model tab, fv scorecard window

entries.short: An input goes into an FV model only if it cuts held-out error.
body: Hockey, soccer and tennis: t >= 2 across held-out classes, seasons or birth years, and it wins two thirds of them.
CBB: dropping the driver has to raise out-of-sample deviance in 4 of 5 folds, with whole players held out.
CFB: the multipliers are refit leaving one draft class out, and a driver stays only if the within-position r with NFL AV improves.
entries.where: fv model tabs (drivers kept, out-of-sample evidence)

entries.short: The CFB model grades every FBS and FCS player on his NFL outcome.
body: The composite is production (Stat+, Marcel 5/4/3, regressed), On3 talent, age, frame, combine, badges and the XV parts.
A player's composite rank in his class maps to FV through measured NFL outcome counts at each position (drafts 2012-18).
The scouting consensus (9 boards and the Kiper top 25) is blended in at a weight of .5 at full coverage.
Then comes the outcome step (ordered probit), the mean headline and the stretched top. Positional value scales elite RB, LB, DL, TE and S.
entries.where: CFB board, draft board, fv model tab

entries.short: The CBB model grades every D-I player and listed international on his NBA outcome.
body: E[FV] = 20 + 10 P(30+) + 10 P(40+) + 10 P(50+) + (mean 60+ career - 50) P(60+), with one ridge logistic for each rung.
Newcomers are graded on recruit rank (On3, 247, Barttorvik) and class. Returners add 3-season BPM, conference power, age, size and rates.
The board stage adds the June draft-board rank and guard combine testing. E maps to a grade on the pooled 2009-16 boards.
The outcome odds are fit on each board's top 300. Below that they scale down to the floor those boards realized (1.8% NBA).
In season, E = (1 - w) × preseason + w × now, with w = minutes / (minutes + k). k is 85 for newcomers and 156 for returners.
entries.where: CBB board, fv model tab, in season window

entries.short: An OLS on outcome FV for the draft class and for drafted players short of 100 NHL games.
body: The draft model keeps log slot (board rank as slot), defense, goalie, draft-year NHLe, class strength.
Leave-one-class-out error is 87.92, compared to 92.44 for draft slot alone (2008-19 classes, 2,541 picks).
After the draft, stage models add the latest NHLe, pro games, a World Juniors spot, NHL games and WAR so far.
entries.where: Hockey prospects board, drafted prospects, fv model tab

entries.short: An OLS on outcome FV for every under-22 in 33 leagues, plus academy and feeder leagues.
body: The inputs kept include age, market value (deflated to the level of the fit seasons), GAR this season and last,
minutes share, club strength, scoring rate, height, position and PL2 minutes. 53,682 rows, 2013-20.
The detailed position block (centre-back, full-back, defensive and attacking midfield, winger and striker, against central
midfield) cuts season-out error by -0.10 (t = 3.9, 7 of 8 seasons), and the top 50 and forward tests are better too.
The raw grade is the mean of the OLS grade and a gradient-boosted grade (300 trees of depth 3 on every design input,
one set for each snapshot). Season-out error goes from 55.62 to 54.62 (t = 8.7, 8 of 8 seasons). The trees get no missing-height
signal, and they see market values only as dated on a player's own lineups.
Held out by birth cohort, the error is 54.84, compared to 64.42 for age and market value alone (R² .43).
entries.where: Soccer prospects board, fv model tab

entries.short: A hurdle model for every ATP and WTA player under 22 with a ranking or a pro match in the last year.
body: A logistic for any peak value, then an OLS on outcome FV given value: FV = (1 - p) × 20 + p × mean given value.
ATP keeps age, rank, unranked, Elo, 52-week win rate, years since the pro debut and Futures volume.
WTA keeps age, rank, unranked, Elo, rank × age and tour-qualifying volume. Held out by birth year, OOS R² is .50 / .46.
Height is never an input, since the archive fills in height for the players who made it, which leaks the outcome.
The ATP fit also trains on unfinished careers (later births at imputed targets): as-of 2011-18 error goes from 21.45 to 20.24, t = 7.8, 8 of 8.

An ATP tree blend (the mean with a boosted-tree grade) went from 20.24 to 19.86 as of, t = 2.7, 7 of 8, p .015. It was a second form after the first failed, so it counts in the sweep's Holm family of 15 and misses the cut (p <= .005). It isn't used. The WTA trees failed going forward.
entries.where: Tennis prospects ATP and WTA boards, fv model tab

entries.short: Projected RWA over the next year against tier-1 starters, on the 20-80 scale (50 = an average tier-1 starter).
body: A prospect is a player under 20 with maps at S-tier events. The projection uses rating, age and the share of last year's rounds at S/A-tier events.
The S/A share is negative on top of the rating's tier lift (held t = -4.9). Rise and every stat line failed.
Cutoffs are quarterly, fit on 2024-25 and held out from Jul 2025. A term ships only if it clears the Bonferroni cut for its batch.
Badges (top 25% on a stat) were tested on prospects and on the main board. None passed, so CS2 shows none.

entries.short: The baseball boards are graded by hand on the FanGraphs 20-80 tiers.
body: There is no model. 80 is top 5 overall (7+ WAR a season), 60 is an All-Star (3.4-4.9) and 50 is an average regular (1.6-2.4).
Boards: 2026 draft hitters v1, U19 MiLB prospects and the White Sox org top 64.
entries.where: Baseball page (draft hitters, U19 MiLB, White Sox org, fv scale)

entries.short: Projected FV for high school recruits.
body: CFB xFV = P(on board) × FV if on + (1 - P(on)) × 20, in year 1, from a hurdle fit on the ESPN 2023-26 classes.
The CFB recruit profile is weighted on the NFL outcomes of the 2011-19 classes, and the board sets the level.
CBB uses a hurdle on consensus rank and old-for-class: P(reach NBA), then log(FV - 20) given NBA, trained on 2009-16.
entries.where: Recruits tabs: 2027-2029 classes, class rankings, recruit model

entries.short: A recruit star rating cut on what past recruits with the same profile became, instead of the industry stars.
body: CFB is cut on the recruit index (expected NFL outcome, 2011-19 classes). A class holds about 34 five-stars, 102 four-stars and 265 three-stars.
Share drafted in CFB, held out: 5-star+ 79%, 5-star 55%, 4-star 29%, 3-star 18%, 2-star 9%, 1-star 3%.
CBB is cut on FV. 5 = 2+ NBA seasons as a starter, 4 = reached the NBA, 3 = a D-I starter at BPM +3, 2 = played D-I, 1 = did not.
There are half stars inside each tier. The arrow is ARK stars minus industry stars.

entries.short: The tier above five stars, for recruits at even odds or better of the top pro outcome.
body: CFB: a five-star with a 50%+ chance of a top-64 pick. There are about 6 a class. Held out, 57% went top 64 and 79% were drafted (plain five-stars 29% and 55%).
The chance reads the recruit index, the log industry rank and the industry rating past 95. Held out by class 2011-21: school-clustered t = 2.22, 9/11 classes. The 2022 class has 4 of 4 top-64.
Top-64 rate for the top 3 of a class: 79% with the industry terms, 58% on the index alone and 70% on industry rank. Top 6: 55%, 52%, 55%.
CBB: FV 41.43+, about 5 a class. Held out, 62% became NBA starters (2+ seasons) and 42% reached FV 55+ (plain five-stars 26%).

The CBB line was re-tested on the same even-odds rule. A line at FV 43.5 (3.2 a class) hits 69%, but the recruits between the two lines hit 50% and the six-tier R² falls from 0.318 to 0.297, so the line stays.
Position at the top failed in both: CFB quarterback and line flags t = -0.63, CBB big and point guard flags t = -0.92.

entries.short: A recruit's age on Sep 1 of the class year, minus the class median. Positive means old for the class.
body: The median is 18.84 in CBB (1,723 ranked recruits 2009-16) and 18.67 in CFB (1,415 top-400 recruits who reached the NFL).
CBB NBA rate at about the same rank: 38% under 17.9, 31% at 18.2-18.6 and 18% at 19.0+.
The CBB model input is old for the class (18+ on Oct 26 of the senior year), held out t = 2.65, 6/8 classes.
Continuous age in its place is t = 1.19, added on top t = 1.20, and a young flag t = 0.84 (gate 2.0). None of them shipped.
CFB top-64 pick rate given an NFL entry: 28% at 18.0-18.4 and 20% at 19.2+. Draft slot t = 1.75, 6/9.
CFB doesn't use it. It is short of the gate, and On3 lists an age for 34 of the top 300 in the latest class read.
Birth dates come from On3's whole-year age, bounded tighter by each daily reading, plus FIBA youth rosters and pins.
Cards show age against the class once the birth date is known to within 45 days. Hockey late birthdays and soccer birth month failed.

entries.short: A class's commits' FV points over the floor, summed. Top end and depth are its two parts.
body: CFB sums xFV - 20 and CBB sums expected FV points. Top end is the best 5 commits in CFB and the best 2 in CBB, and depth is the rest.

Both parts were tested against results: program rating z, with the ratings before signing, a three-season baseline and program level as controls, held out and clustered by program. Reweightings were pre-registered: split, decay by rank in class, cap, star premium (points to a power), average + size, power x decay.

CFB, the four classes on a roster (2013-25, n = 1,605): the sum beats no class score at t = 3.49, 13 of 13 seasons. A top-end point is worth 0.0044 rating SD (SE 0.0015) and a depth point 0.0027 (SE 0.0011), difference t = 0.70.
Per standard deviation that is 0.17 rating SD for top end and 0.11 for depth. Raw correlation with the season's rating: 0.54 and 0.43; after the controls 0.24 and 0.23.

No CFB reweighting beats the sum: split t = -1.59, decay t = -0.52, cap t = -1.82, star premium t = -0.20, power x decay t = -2.15. One class at a time (2012-22, n = 1,357) the best is t = 0.03. Quarterback and line points next to the sum: t = -3.09.

CBB, one class at a time (2012-23, n = 1,342): discounting depth looks better (power x decay t = 2.52, 9 of 12 classes) and a depth point reads -0.0084. That is roster turnover: a deep freshman class follows a thin returning roster.

With returning and transfer value held fixed (first season, n = 1,546), a CBB top-end point is worth 0.0071 (SE 0.0022) and a depth point 0.0049 (SE 0.0028), difference t = 0.51, and every discount loses: decay t = -1.03, cap t = -2.47, star premium t = 0.19, power x decay t = -1.32.
CBB rating bends with the class total (diminishing returns, t = 4.40), which changes no class's order. CFB does not bend (t = 0.31).

The sum stays the class score in both sports, and top end and depth stay descriptive ranks. Lead: in NIL-era CFB seasons a top-end point is worth 0.0069 and a depth point 0.0006 (t = 1.49, n = 511); retest after the 2027 season.
Second pass, same test. Another value basis does not beat the one in use: CFB FV if on the board t = 0.09 and year-3 xFV t = -1.06; CBB headline FV t = 1.28 and Y1 FV t = -0.48. Blends fail too.
Program development times the sum: CFB t = -1.91, CBB t = 0.77. Early and late commits weighted apart: t = -1.20 and -0.40. CBB enrol rate of the three classes before: t = 0.79.

Incoming transfers next to the class, first season: CBB passes at t = 6.45, 12 of 13 classes (NIL era t = 4.76). A unit of transfer value is worth 7.8 class points, and per standard deviation transfers move the rating 0.17 SD to the class's 0.08. CFB incoming transfer production: t = 0.73.

That is a net class (high school commits plus transfers), not a change to the high school score. Not testable on stored history: positional need against the returning roster, decommit risk, per-recruit Transfer% and Ret%.
History points are the live model's by composite rating and level (CFB) or consensus rank (CBB); against the live class scores r = 0.966 and 0.997.
entries.where: Recruits tabs: class rankings; class rankings GFX

entries.short: Bronze to platinum trait medals next to the name, each on one stat, regressed by volume.
body: The tiers are the 75th, 90th, 97th and 99th percentile of the position. CFB badges build archetypes.
On the other boards a badge shows only if it predicts the sport's own outcome held out, beyond the value metric.
They are display only, and no badge feeds FV or a projection. Volume and usage traits pass, and efficiency rates mostly fail.
entries.where: Every board (medals by the name), player cards

entries.short: Each player's grade at his best season, listed by position.
body: CFB rebuilds every FBS season 2014-25, with the box-score era (2014-18) means recalibrated to NFL outcomes.
The CFB outcome is NFL AV a season since the draft over a class horizon index h (mean 1 on the 2020-23 drafts), so years an old class spent out of the league don't count against it.
The other boards read their past lists, and only grade-complete rows are used.
entries.where: all-time FV tab on CFB, CBB, hockey, soccer and tennis prospect pages

entries.short: Wins over a replacement starter in a 12-game season.
body: WAR = snap share × (line + weight × quality) × .227. One point of margin a game is worth .0189 win% (928 FBS team seasons).
The line is the margin a team loses when an average starter sits: QB 2.7, RB 1.7, EDGE 1.4, WR 1.35, CB 1.3, S 1.1, DT 1.0, LB 1.0.
Quality comes from Stat+, badges and FV. The QB keeps 1.25 points per SD, and the rest goes to his offensive teammates by snaps.
A replacement lineup wins .18 (2 of 12), and an average team's starters add up to 3.8 WAR.
In team WAR, starter time that no graded player covers counts one SD below an average starter (season AV's line), instead of at
the WAR line. Held out by season 2019 to 2025, team WAR tracks SRS at R² .654, compared to .639 (t = 3.5, 7 of 7 seasons).
entries.where: CFB board, WAR leaders tab, team talent

entries.short: WAR minus snap share × line, which is wins over an average starter at the position.
body: It compares across positions, and a below-average starter is below 0.

entries.short: WAR with quality taken from the parts of the stat line that track winning.
body: CFB: the PFN score plus position parts (QB cmp %, yds/att and INT rate, OL pressure rate, DT splash, CB yds/target).
It is fit on 2024-25 team margin. Held out, team r is .88 compared to .86 for WAR quality, and win% r is .73 compared to .68.
NFL: the same idea, fit to team margin a game. On missed games it is t = 4.9, compared to 2.1 for AV WAR.
Next-season forecasts tie with WAR, so the projections and the game models stay on WAR.
The NFL weights are fit for each side: offense parts on points scored a game, and defense parts on points allowed a game.
XV from weeks 1 to 9 on the margin from week 10 on goes from R² .604 to .622 (t = 2.19, 7 of 8 seasons), and next-season team R² from .235 to .258.
Held out, XV is the most descriptive NFL metric (.604, compared to .401 for WAR and .257 for SV) and the most descriptive CFB one (.689, compared to .639 for cWAR).
entries.where: CFB and NFL WAR leaders tabs (XV column)

entries.short: Wins over replacement, .6 × AV WAR + .4 × XV, season to date.
body: AV WAR = (AV - replacement AV at the sub-position × snap share) × .091 wins per AV.
The .091 comes from team wins on team AV (160 team seasons 2021-25, r .86). A replacement team wins 3 of 17.
Defensive AV is rebuilt from pressures, stops and plays on the ball. Two-way players earn WAR on each side.
entries.where: NFL WAR leaders, team WAR, rookies, standouts

entries.short: A production index: 100 + 25 × z of the position's all-in-one score this season.
body: The source scores are PFN QB+, RB+, WR+, TE+, OLi, EDGE+, DT+, LB+, CB+ and SAF+, with K and P by percentile.
z is against the snap-weighted position mean, FBS or FCS, so 125 is 1 SD above average.
It is an FV production driver. Validity against NFL AV: TE .52, WR .50, QB .48, RB .48, EDGE .40, LB .40, DT .37.
entries.where: CFB board, WAR leaders, true freshmen

entries.short: xNIL is what a player is worth on the NIL market now, yNIL is his estimated pay entering the season, and zNIL = xNIL - yNIL.
body: xNIL = position price × on-field value (AV at FV, × playing time), shared within the P4 and G5 pools.
yNIL splits each program's budget by a preseason index. The budget is the school's reported one: 68 P4 football programs (mean $27.2M) and 80 high-major basketball programs (mean $13.7M).
Without a report it is assumed: $3M in the G5, $0.4M in the FCS, $1.2M for a mid-major and $0.25M for a low-major in basketball.

The budget pays the whole roster. A provisionally graded football backup is paid 5% of the median graded player at his position on the team, and a kicker or punter 20% of the team's median graded player, rising 10% per FV point. Both shares were set on the College Sports Commission's pay percentiles. Their xNIL shares the group's own pay by worth, so a backup's or a specialist's zNIL is against his group's going rate.

A reported deal (6 on file) moves the player half way from the model's number to the report: his yNIL when the deal is for this season, his xNIL when it was reported in the last year. It also enters the price fit, so a position's price follows the reports between On3's repricings. On3 moved toward each of the three reports it trailed.
A budget list from an earlier season is carried forward at the market's growth (11% a year).
It isn't fit to On3 valuations, since those only move +18% per 10 FV. zNIL growth is 20% of each coach score.
Checked against the College Sports Commission's pay percentiles by position, On3 valuations and reported deals.
FCS players at an FBS-starter FV are priced at 40% of the FBS rate. CBB xNIL is minutes share × (BPM + 3) at the school's price.
entries.where: CFB board, team talent, team builder, fv to xNIL charts; CBB recruits

entries.short: A college player's on-field value for a season: snap share × position weight × quality.
body: Quality = Stat+ z + .5 badge z + .25 FV z. Team R² against 2026 SRS is .63, compared to .44 for summed FV value.
It is used for the cost of college injuries and for team value. NFL value stays on AV at FV.
entries.where: CFB team talent (Season AV), fv to war chart

entries.short: XPM (Cross Plus-Minus) is an NBA impact metric, .5 databallr DPM + .5 Basketball-Reference BPM, in points per 100 possessions over an average player, as played.
body: It is the headline XPM on every NBA board. O-XPM and D-XPM are the same blend for each side.
It includes BPM's team adjustment. Every player on a team moves by one amount on each side, so that minutes-weighted O-XPM × 5 = ORtg - league and D-XPM × 5 = league - DRtg.
Same-season team net R² is 0.999 (the box blend before the adjustment 0.963, BPM 0.988). Next season it is 0.647 (box blend 0.640, BPM 0.644).
The box blend before the adjustment feeds pXPM, the game models (which shrink it themselves) and the CBB board target. A player with no DPM row uses BPM alone (*).
The XPM and rookie boards default to qualified players, 1,000 MP per 82 team games. For qualified rookies 2010-23, XPM orders next-three-season VORX at .607 (VORX .604), and .330 for all rookies.
entries.where: NBA VORX/XPM leaders, rookies, team pages, ARKLIST

entries.short: Projected XPM for next season: XPM over three seasons by minutes, shrunk toward a role mean and aged. On the depth charts and backup watch it shrinks toward replacement.
body: Boards: (k × role mean + MP × XPM + w1 × MP-1 × XPM-1 + w2 × MP-2 × XPM-2) / (k + MP + w1 MP-1 + w2 MP-2) + the aging curve to next season.
k 200 MP, w1 0.35, w2 0.1, role mean = -3 + 1 ln(1 + MP82 / 100). Aging is the next-season change in XPM by age, fit on earlier seasons only.
Next-season XPM 2011-26, leaving one season out: RMSE 1.187, compared to 1.238 for a one-dial k 600 shrink and 1.58 raw (t = -7.28, 14/15 seasons).
Next-season team net rating, nine pairs, held out: R² 0.654, against rXPM 0.640, BPM 0.644, DPM 0.623 and the k 600 shrink 0.619.
Depth chart and backup watch: XPM over three seasons (minutes weighted 1, .5, .25) × M / (M + 500) + replacement (-1.4) × 500 / (M + 500).
entries.where: NBA VORX/XPM leaders (pXPM chip), rookies, depth chart, backup watch

entries.short: VORX (Value Over Replacement XPM) is NBA wins over replacement: .030 × (XPM + 1.4) × MP / 48.
body: Replacement is -1.4 XPM. Both constants are fit to team wins (480 team seasons 2011-26). It is the default sort on the XPM and rookie boards.

Team W% from minutes-weighted value, 2011-26: same-season R² is 0.938 on XPM, compared to 0.926 on the box blend before the team adjustment (t = 2.33, 10/13 seasons). Next season it is 0.679 compared to 0.681 (t = -0.25).
For rookies 2010-23, held out, VORX orders next-three-season VORX best (Spearman .398; pXPM .395, aXPM .379, XPM .330).
For next-three-season XPM, the rookie 3Y orders it best (.481; aXPM .413, XPM .417, VORX .351).
entries.where: NBA VORX/XPM leaders, projections, contract value

entries.short: MD is the points per 100 matchup possessions a defender's assignments scored against everyone. PAOE is what they scored against him minus MD, shrunk by poss / (poss + 300).
body: The source rows are one defender on one offensive player in one game (NBA.com box score matchups via shufinskiy/nba_data),
with partial possessions and points. Each assignment's season rate is pulled toward the league by 100 possessions.
Defenders need 1,000+ partial possessions. The odd/even game reliability of PAOE at 1,000+ possessions is r .82 (2017-18 to 2025-26).
As a prior-season team-defence input, PAOE did not help (team net RMSE 3.528 compared to 3.525, held 2023-26 t = +0.13), so it is display only.

entries.short: Projected XPM next season (given he plays) and over the next three (× the chance he plays in them).
body: It is built from XPM (proj), age, projected minutes, a hinge above +3 and the two seasons before, with coefficients by the share of the season played.
Given he plays, it is fit on seasons with minutes, weighted by them. Held out 2012-23 at 1,000+ minutes, 3Y RMSE is 1.13 and 1Y is 1.14.
3Y = stay × XPM given he plays + (1 - stay) × -2. Stay is the chance he plays in the next three seasons (XPM, age, minutes, games).
Held out 2012-23 (6,165 player seasons, 18% out of the league), RMSE goes from 2.81 to 2.78 (t = -4.4, 11/12 seasons).
It is display only.

entries.short: Season-to-date XPM blended with a preseason prior by minutes.
body: prior + (XPM - prior) × MP / (k + MP), with k 509 for veterans and 809 for newcomers (7,269 player seasons 2012-26).
The 80% range covers .806 / .799 held out. It is display only.

entries.short: Minimum salary + projected VORX × the market price of a win, minus salary, for every year left on the deal.
body: The price of a win is payroll above the minimum divided by the league's projected VORX, refit on every update, rising 7% a year (an assumption).
A player option counts only when it pays the player, and a team option only when it pays the team.

entries.short: The AAV a player would sign for as a free agent now, as a share of the cap from position, age and his last full season.
body: It is fit on real signings and held out a signing year at a time against the mean by position × age. The forms were pre-registered, and the live form is the lowest held-out MAE whose top end is calibrated (players priced at 7%+ of the cap signed for 85-115% of it). It models the square root of the cap share, smeared back, and is clipped to the league minimum and maximum.

NHL: 3,241 CapWages deals 2010-26 (standard, 35+ and two-way, no ELCs or extensions), on WAR, pWAR, 3Y, points and TOI a game, games and age, by F/D/G. MAE is .83% of the cap compared to 1.70 (t = -40, 17/17 seasons, forward 11/11). Points and TOI alone tie it (t = -1.4), so the market pays for points.

NFL: 12,192 OverTheCap veteran contracts 2014-26 (3+ years after the draft), on WAR the last two seasons, snaps, games and age, by position. MAE is .86% compared to 1.50 (t = -52, 13/13, forward 9/9). WAR adds over snaps alone (t = -18). The ceiling is the record 24.5% (Burrow 2023).

NBA: 1,334 Basketball-Reference offseason signings 2011-26 (free agent, multi-year or plain contracts, with next season's salary on the signing team), on XPM the last two seasons, VORX, minutes, points and minutes a game, games, age and years in the league. MAE is 2.60% compared to 5.04 (t = -19, 16/16, forward 11/11). XPM and VORX add over points and minutes alone (t = -6, 14/16). The max is 25/30/35% by years in the league, and the 2026-27 cap is $165M (projected).
Soccer isn't built. There is no public wage data I can reach (Capology blocks it), and xMV is the transfer-market equivalent.
I also scored the NHL version against AFP Analytics' public projections, on the 109 signings of summer 2026 that both priced (ours from a fit on earlier years only,
AFP's dated May 18 2026). Our mean miss was 1.03% of the cap, compared to .77 for AFP (t = +2.7 against ours).
Restricted free agents were 1.52 compared to .85 (n 30), and unrestricted .81 compared to .70 (n 73). xAAV has no free-agent status input.
entries.where: NBA, NFL, NHL contract value tabs

entries.short: The contract length, in years, a player would sign for as a free agent now.
body: It uses the same inputs and signings as xAAV (3,242 CapWages deals 2010-26), linear in years and clipped 1-8.
Held out a signing year at a time, the mean miss is .83 years, compared to 1.00 by position × age (t = -13.0, 16/17 years),
and forward 2016-26 it is .82 compared to 1.01 (t = -12.2, 11/11).
Surplus = (xAAV - cap hit) × seasons left on the current deal.

entries.short: Projected XPM this season, the board's projection for every player, freshmen and transfers included.
body: A ridge on last season, recruiting, age and size, with rXPM (CBB) as the target. Returners also take pXPM (CBB), board form. In season it blends in XPM to date.
Team context: returning teammates' VORX, teammates' recruiting (top 8, -ln rank), WAA and transferring up or down.
It was xBPM, the same ridge with BPM as the target and no pXPM. Walk-forward 2012-13 to 2025-26, next-season team R² over the whole roster goes from .7718 to .7768 (14/14, t = 7.81).

For returners, pXPM added moves it from .7348 to .7406 (t = 12.05). The box form of pXPM alone is t = 1.67, and the rXPM target alone is t = 1.39. For newcomers the target swap is a tie (t = 1.94 scored on XPM).
The fit rows read pXPM point in time, from a refit that walks forward a season at a time.
As xBPM, forward 2020-26, RMSE went from 2.558 to 2.462 for returners (t = 18) and from 3.439 to 3.229 for newcomers (t = 14) with team context. It is not an FV input.
entries.where: CBB board hover, true freshmen, standouts, draft board, team talent, team builder

entries.short: XPM for a college season: Barttorvik BPM's split of credit inside the team, on team totals that track wins.
body: For each side, rXPM = BPM + the team's minutes-weighted mean of (GBPM - BPM). GBPM is the minutes-weighted mean of his games' BPM (Barttorvik).
Team totals equal GBPM's, and the gaps between teammates equal BPM's.

Team totals, 2007-08 to 2025-26: wins above bubble a game R² is .888 compared to .880 for BPM (t = 11.3, 19/19), and win% is .676 compared to .652 (19/19). On adjusted margin, which is BPM's own anchor, it is .9954 compared to .9996.

The split inside the team is tested on who sat out: game margin, adjusted for opponent and site, minus the team's season mean, on the minutes-weighted rating of the players who played, with ratings from the other games.
Against GBPM: all rotation players t = 3.03 (14/19), starters t = 4.85 (17/19), split halves t = 1.89 (11/19). Against BPM it is identical.
Next season, which isn't its job, team R² is .624, GBPM .611 (t = 3.37) and BPM .642. pXPM is the projection.
SD 3.62 (BPM 3.81), r with BPM .998, mean gap .24.
Failed held out: O/D blends of BPM and GBPM, college box weights fit to who sat out, wins or capped-margin anchors, and GBPM moved toward raw net rating (a schedule artifact).

As a model input in place of BPM it failed held out: the ten award voter models (t = -1.48 to .36), Transfer% (t = -5.09), Ret% (t = -.19) and the school development outcome (rolling gain 2.50% on BPM, 2.04% on rXPM). Those stay on BPM. Award conviction and the stats shown beside the awards use XPM.
entries.where: CBB board (XPM), VORX/XPM leaders, stats, portal, award conviction, all-time list

entries.short: Projected XPM next season on offense and defense, from three seasons of box lines plus team and recruit ratings.
body: For each side: (K × mean of sub-200-minute players + minutes × BPM, with the last three seasons weighted 1 / w1 / w2) / (K + weighted minutes),
then a fit on next-season BPM from that history, ln minutes, class, and twelve box rates z-scored within the season × minutes / (minutes + 200)
(steal, block, OREB, DREB, assist, turnover, FT rate, 3PA/100, rim share, usage, TS, height), with a ridge of 10 on the rates.
O: w .35 / .2, K 200. D: w .6 / .4, K 100. Fit on next-season minutes, 2008-09 to 2025-26 pairs (in the research form below, D took 25% GBPM).
Walk-forward 2012-13 to 2025-26: next-season team adjEM R² is .732 compared to .642 for BPM (14/14, t = 15.7). Player r is .770 compared to .680, and RMSE 2.36 compared to 3.41.
xXPM, the board's projection, takes the board form as an input next to recruiting and team context: for returners, team R² is .741 and player r .794.

In the roster prior, in place of last-season BPM, next-season team R² goes from .757 to .765 (13/14, t = 4.08). Game margin MAE goes from 9.2643 to 9.2618 in 2016-20 (t = -2.55) and from 9.5915 to 9.5892 in 2021-26 (t = -2.76). xBPM fails there (t = -3.18).

As an FV returner driver, it adds +.57% out of sample (t = 3.42, 5/5), and in place of 3-season BPM t = 2.48. Nested pseudo-R² goes from .105 to .107, RPS from .0802 to .0789, and the 2017-19 top 50 from 39.0 to 39.6.
In NBA mock conviction, in place of 3-season BPM, it is t = .6 (8/15 drafts), so 3-season BPM stays.
The board form adds team context (5 × the minutes-weighted mean side BPM of his team / 10; O .42, D .15) and recruit rating / 100 by class (Fr O .68 D .50, So .58 / .31, Jr+ .26 / .34).
Walk-forward, team R² goes from .733 to .746 (13/14, t = 7.87), against .642 for BPM (14/14, t = 15.3). Player r is .780 and RMSE 2.32.

On their own, team context is t = 7.07 and recruit rating t = 4.95. Late-season form, age, role and freshman height, minutes share and its change, and game BPM consistency failed (t = -5.22 to 2.38 alone, and nothing once the two are in).
The board form in the roster prior goes from .765 to .768 (13/14, t = 3.74). As the FV driver in place of the box form it is t = .87.

Through the game model, the board form moves held-out margin MAE (2021-26) from 9.5892 to 9.5903 (t = 2.5, worse in 11/11 seasons), and 9.5594 against 9.5601 with the prior weight retuned. In FV, nested R² goes from .107 to .114, but the top-300 correlation with outcome on the 2017-19 boards goes from .386 to .377 and RPS from .0789 to .0791. FV, the roster prior and the game model stay on the box form.

The board form also goes into the next-season value column (Next) in place of last-season BPM in the roster row: RMSE goes from 30.17 to 29.19 (t = 22.0, 11/11 seasons), and in season it replaces 3-season BPM at every share of the season played (t = 13.07 to 25.58).
Added to next up odds as the gap between pXPM and the shrunk value, the Brier score goes from .2077 to .2050 (t = 5.1, 16/16).

In Transfer%, in place of BPM, log loss goes from .8999 to .8862 and AUC from .710 to .725 (t = 6.49). In the landing spot model the right school is in the top 10 16.4% of the time, up from 15.1% (t = 5.95).
In the depth chart and backup watch grade it replaces last season's BPM (t = 45.15 to 63.87, 12/12 seasons at every share of the season).
It failed in Ret% (t = .75), and in NBA mock conviction (t = -1.44, 2/15 drafts). The same gap added to NBA next up odds is t = 1.42, so it isn't there.
The descriptive counterpart is rXPM (CBB).
entries.where: CBB pXPM leaders, portal, board hover; box form: FV (returners), roster prior / game model

entries.short: Wins over a replacement or an average D-I player.
body: VORX = (sXPM + 1.4) × minutes / 40 × 68 possessions a 40 / 100 × .0187 wins a point. WAA uses sXPM alone.
XPM is rXPM (CBB), and sXPM = (XPM × min + 100 × season mean) / (min + 100).
Replacement is 1.4 below average, the 9th man's sXPM in 2025-26. Wins a point is fit on 3,485 team seasons 2017-26:
wins = .39 × games + team VORX (r .87). It is season only, so no earlier season enters a season's VORX.
GBPM over season BPM moved held-out team win% R² from .633 to .658, 15 of 15 seasons. The shrink cut half-B GBPM MSE from 16.2 to 11.4
(10 of 10) and held-out team wins RMSE from 3.348 to 3.331 (14 of 14). rXPM then replaced GBPM, with the same team totals and BPM's split inside the team.
The textbook slope (.0347 at a margin sd of 11.5) overstates it, since schedules pair strong teams with strong teams and win odds flatten at the ends.
In the FV test, VORX, WAA, career VORX and 5/4/3 VORX all fail.
It is the same value over replacement as NBA VORX, on the college scale. It was called WAR here before.
entries.where: CBB VORX/XPM leaders, stats, portal, returning

entries.short: XPM against the position, 100 + 25 × z.
body: z = (XPM - position mean) / position sd. The tabs use last season's norms (G -.25 / 3.62, F .53 / 3.90, C 1.64 / 4.34),
then this season's own once 40 players at a position qualify. The FV driver is on BPM, with norms G .10 / 3.85, F .50 / 4.05, C .52 / 4.31 (2008-16).
As an FV driver it passes all three fold rules (t = 2.9-3.5, 4-5/5), and it held in 2017-19 (+.17) and forward in 2020-23 (+.26).
entries.where: CBB stats, WAR leaders, portal; FV inputs

entries.short: Hollinger's single-game value.
body: PTS + .4 FGM - .7 FGA - .4 (FTA - FTM) + .7 ORB + .3 DRB + STL + .7 AST + .7 BLK - .4 PF - TOV.
Every FV and xXPM test failed (a game, a 40, best game, 20+ games).

entries.short: First and second-year players playing above their preseason projection.
body: xXPM up = live xXPM - preseason xXPM (minutes-blended). The tab also shows XPM over x, minutes, usage and FV gains.
The last season view puts second-years against their freshman line (VORX, XPM, minutes and usage gains).
In the FV tests, VORX gain, minutes gain, usage gain and BPM × (1 - minutes share) all fail. Low-minute BPM passes the folds, but not at the top of the board.

entries.short: Team tables for how much of last season's minutes and VORX is back, and roster grades.
body: Ret Min% is the share of last season's minutes still on the roster (Barttorvik ids). In VORX is the VORX of incoming transfers.
Talent is the mean FV of the top 8. xNBA is the sum of NBA%. TvE is talent rank minus ARK rank.
In the FV tests, vacated minutes (opportunity), returning teammates' VORX and teammates' recruiting fail. The last two pass for xXPM.

entries.short: The CBB FV target, the mean of a career's best three NBA XPM seasons, each shrunk toward -2 by 500 minutes.
body: Each FV band starts at the XPM that as many careers reached as reached the matching NBA role. See the CBB chart.

entries.short: Descriptive wins over replacement, at goal value.
body: 5v5 on-ice xG against teammates, PP xG / 5, PK / 4, finishing (goals - ixG), penalties, and a share of the team's leftover xG.
Goalies get GSAx at full credit. It sums to team goal differential (R² .991).
Replacement is the level of players outside each team's top 13 F, 7 D and 2 G.

entries.short: Projected WAR, and projected goals per 60 over an average player.
body: HPM is Marcel-weighted (1 / .5 / .25) shrunk rates, with each component weighted by how well it carries to the next season.
pWAR = (HPM - replacement) × TOI / 60 / goals per win. Leave one season out, R² is .37 compared to .26 before (t = 4.24, 15/17 seasons).
Goalie GSAx barely repeats (weight .21), so goalie pWAR is about 0.4 while goalie WAR runs about 7.
5 on 5 on-ice and individual xG read MoneyPuck's flurry, score and venue adjusted columns. WAR keeps raw xG.
Next-season team GD R² goes from .384 to .387 (t = 2.88, 13 of 17 pairs). With the weights refit, held out it goes from .373 to .376, walk-forward t = 3.59.
PP on-ice xG at a weight of .2 fails (t = 1.19 worse), and score and venue alone is flat (t = .32).
entries.where: NHL WAR leaders, backup watch, rookies; hockey prospect outcome (skaters)

entries.short: Goals saved above expected (MoneyPuck xG).
body: The goalie tab shows GSAx a game, shrunk toward a new goalie's level. It feeds the NHL totals model.

entries.short: NHL points over a full season, at a league's translation factor.
body: The factors are fit on every pick's career since 2008 from league pairs, with a year of age development taken out.
They are shrunk toward the published factor by link count. CHL leagues sit around .10-.12, and the NCAA around .21.

entries.short: Goals above replacement, on one scale across leagues.
body: Shrunk per-90 rates (on-pitch xG for and against, on-off, npxG, xGBuildup, keeper saves) plus an xG plus-minus (offence, defence),
weighted to next-season team goal difference.
On-pitch xG and xGBuildup are adjusted for opponent and home: minus what that club allowed in its other matches, shrunk,
and the league's home / away gap. On odd against even matches of a player-season, held 2022-26, on-pitch xG for goes from r .65 to .70,
against from .45 to .54 and buildup from .64 to .65. A player's own npxG and xA gain .003 to .006, so they stay raw.
The xG plus-minus is a weighted ridge over 3 seasons of on-pitch spells (the same 22 on the field):
a spell's npxG a 90 on the attacking side's players (offence) and the defending side's (defence), with league-season and home terms.
Offence is shrunk toward his xG + xA a 90 over the window, and defence toward 0.
Replacement for each position is the regulars (900+ minutes) on the bottom three sides by goal difference of each finished league-season,
pooled, less the sides that collapsed (second-half points a match under .6 and below their first half; 42 of 180, Nov 27 2026).
Their regulars sat .02 a 90 under the rest of the bottom three. Without them the line sits closer to what free signings and academy
call-ups (t -7.3, 11/11 seasons) and promoted sides' regulars (t -3.3, 9/11) produce the next season up, held out. Season to season the line
moves .010 to .018 a 90 by position, 0.3 to 0.5 GAR for a 30-match regular. Lines by role (FB, CB, DM, CM, AM, W, ST) matched promoted
sides better (t -7.4) but not free signings (6/11), so the line stays GK, D, M, F; the board shows the role.
League strength counts. Held out R² is .686 (.673 before the plus-minus; nested test t = -2.97, 9/11 seasons).
PAR = GAR × points per goal of difference (.626).
1Y P20/P80 come from held-out projection residuals in five bands of season share. Left-out seasons hit .200 and .800 (3Y .201, .800).
aGAR/90 (first seasons) = GAR/90 minus .0032 a year of age over 21. It ranks the next two seasons better than GAR/90, .664 compared to .654, t = -2.66.
entries.where: Soccer player value, rookies, backup watch

entries.short: Team-share goals above replacement: minutes / 90 × (club rating - replacement) / 11.
body: Club rating is goals a match against an average big-five club. Replacement is -2.5, a bottom side in Scotland, Greece or Denmark.
The outcome is the mean of the best three tGAR seasons at ages 22-26. It is a different scale from the senior GAR above, about 4-5× larger.

entries.short: Estimated market value in EUR millions, with no market input.
body: A ridge on log Transfermarkt value from GAR now and in the past two seasons, minutes, age, position, league and club,
national-team matchday squads in the last 12 and 24 months, last season's Champions League + Europa League minutes,
and last season's goals over xG and assists over xA.
Held out R² runs from .73 in October to .80 in July. The gap to TM forecasts TM's next move (slope .26 in October,
12/12 seasons) and the summer fee over TM (corr .22, 1,850 sales 2015-22).

entries.short: Elo on every pro match since 1991 at every level, and Elo+ against players the same age.
body: K = 250 / (matches + 5)^0.4, Slams ×1.1, starting at 1500. Elo+ = 100 + 25 per SD against same-age players with 20+ matches.
entries.where: Tennis prospects board, tennis ARK Ranking

entries.short: The round win % a Counter-Strike player adds per round, opponent-adjusted, where 0 is an average tier-1 starter.
body: The box part is the team's round share on its five players' per-round stat lines (kills, deaths, assists, ADR, KAST, openings, trades,
multi-kills, clutches, headshots, damage taken). The plus-minus part is half the round share the box misses, split across the five.
There is no utility measure, since bo3.gg has no flash or utility damage data. Utility $ bought failed (t = -2.5), and accuracy hurt.
Tier lift: +0.5 × the share of last year's rounds at S/A-tier events, since low-tier pools link to the top through few maps.
Opponents are credited ×1.0, with a half-life of 180 days and 25 rounds of shrink. Held out R² is .131, compared to .120 before and .108 for K-D.
Map offsets: each player's decayed residual on each map, shrunk 1,000 rounds toward 0, is added to his RWA on that map.
Held Jul 2025 to Oct 2026, next-month map error goes from .027816 to .027691, t by month 7.0, 15 of 16 months.

entries.short: xMV is the prize money a player adds over replacement for two seasons, xTV is xMV priced on reported buyouts, and team value sums the five.
body: xMV is the prize money a player adds over a replacement-level player in a five with four average tier-1 starters, for two seasons
(aging curve, 15% a year discount). There is no fee data in it. xTV = A × xMV, which is what a buyout should cost. Team value is the current five's xTV summed.
The prize curve is a roster's prize money over the next 182 days on its five's mean RWA against the tier-1 starter mean (VRS top 20),
a Poisson on rating + rating squared, from Valve's VRS prize ledger (every snapshot's top-ten winnings, Feb 2024 on).
Held out from Jul 2025, deviance explained is 0.79, compared to 0.76 for VRS points and 0.81 for both together (rosters only, since players can't carry VRS points).
A and the replacement level (tier-1 mean - q SDs) are fit on 7 reported buyouts (insider/press, unconfirmed; group deals as the sum): A 1.49, q 4.
Leaving one fee out, the typical miss is ×1.60. A flat price per player is ×1.70, and replacement fixed at the VRS 51-100 starters is ×2.33.
A blend toward flat prices (A × xMV^g, g fit) is ×1.69, which fails, so it stays linear.
The reported fees sit near flat and most are Falcons deals, so the values are compressed and at that buyer's prices.
Eternal Fire to Aurora (reported under $2.5M for five) prices at $6.4M, which is a miss. Contracts aren't public and aren't modelled.
Signed is the same value at the first map of the player's current stint (bo3.gg). Stints from before Jul 2024 start there.
Transactions are moves read from map lineups (join, out, core, drop, rebrand, exit). Loans and fees aren't in the lineups.
entries.where: Counter-Strike transfer values, team values, signings

entries.short: Serve and return points won over an average top-100 player, opponent-adjusted.
body: In percentage points, on hard court. xHold and xBreak are games held or broken against an average top-100 opponent, through the game chain.

entries.short: SV (season value) is this season's points a game over a replacement QB (-0.12 EPA a play), opponent-adjusted. Proj is the game model's QB term.
body: SV takes each dropback and QB run, minus how much EPA a play the defense allowed over the league's (in its other games, shrunk with 300 plays): sum(aEPA + 0.12) / games with 10+ plays. Split-half r is .512 raw and .528 adjusted (QB-seasons with 250+ plays, 2021-26). Wind, cold and rain added nothing.

Proj is weighted career EPA/play shrunk toward replacement with 100 pseudo-plays (fit), × the game model's QB coefficient. SV in the game model, as a swap or as an extra term, failed held out 2021-25 (margin MAE from 10.010 to 10.034 / 10.027).

entries.short: SV (season value) is this season's points a game over replacement. Skill players are scored on EPA a run or target, and defenders on credited EPA on plays with negative EPA.
body: Skill (RB, WR, TE): EPA minus the defense's EPA allowed on that play type over the league's (other games, shrunk 300 plays) for RB and WR, and minus the play's weather for RB. Replacement is the level of players past the starters (RB 48, WR 96, TE 48 by volume, 2016-25).

Defenders (DL, LB, DB) split -(EPA minus the offense's rate over the league's; DL, DB) on a sack, INT, pass defensed, forced fumble, TFL, QB hit or a tackle on a failed play. Replacement is the credit a snap past the starters (DL 128, LB 80, DB 160) × snaps.

An adjustment is kept only where split-half r rose (P >= .9): opponent for RB .199 to .217, WR .172 to .190, DL .308 to .315 and DB .147 to .149. TE and LB stay raw. Weather is used only for RB (.217 to .220).
In place of WAR a game in the game model's injury term, it failed held out 2021-25 (MAE from 10.010 to 10.070, 0/5 seasons), so WAR stays.

entries.short: SV (season value) is this season's points a game over replacement from EPA a play (QB: dropbacks and runs; skill players: runs and targets), in FBS games.
body: QB and RB are opponent-adjusted (the defense's EPA allowed on that play type over the league's, other games, shrunk 300 plays): split-half r goes from .360 to .403 for QB and from .179 to .199 for RB. WR and TE stay raw (P .84 / .88 on 2025-26, when target ids are complete). Weather (Open-Meteo at the stadium) added nothing.
Replacement is the level of players past the starters by volume in 2025 (QB 134, RB 268, WR 402, TE 134).
Defenders are left out, since the public plays carry no tackles or snaps and splash credits had no split-half reliability.
In the game model, the starter's adjusted season value scored the same as raw season EPA (t = +0.5), so the QB charge stays.
pSV/60 is SV per 60 plays over three seasons weighted 1, .7, .5, shrunk to the QB mean with 650 plays.
Next-season wMSE goes from .0258 raw to .0159 (t = -11.7, 10 of 10 seasons 2016-25).
entries.where: CFB QB SV + skill players tabs

entries.short: SVAR is SV points over replacement for the season, in wins. It is shown next to WAR, and the models keep WAR.
body: NFL: 36 points a win, the game model's points a win. All-time seasons are put on 17 games (1999-2020 × 17 / 16).
CFB: 53 points a win (FBS win % rises .0189 a point of margin a game over 12 games, from the cfb_war_backtest college fit).

All-time SV history: NFL from 1999 (defenders from 2013, with snap counts) and CFB from 2014 (cfbfastR play-by-play), with CFB WR/TE and RB targets from 2025 (target ids). Replacement moves with each season's league EPA a play, for era.
Every SV test in the game model failed against WAR (NFL QB MAE from 10.010 to 10.034, the NFL non-QB injury term 0/5 seasons, CFB QB = raw), so WAR stays the model input.
entries.where: NFL QBs, skill players, defenders; CFB QB SV, skill players; rookie boards; all-time peak seasons

entries.short: SV (season value) is this season's goals over replacement a 90, from this season alone. SVAR = SV × 90s, the season total in goals. It is shown next to GAR, and the models keep GAR.
body: It uses GAR's weights on this season's inputs only: on-pitch xG for and against, on minus off, npxG, xGBuildup, and an xG plus-minus over this season's spells alone (GAR's spans three seasons). The xG part is scaled ×0.943 so a side's players add up to its xG difference (R² 0.97).

Finishing (goals minus npxG) and keepers' goals saved against xG faced are shrunk toward the league average by min / (min + k), with k 40,000 minutes for saves and 6,000 for finishing, from split-half reliability within a season (odd against even matches: r 0.045 for saves and 0.120 for finishing, with no player prior). A side's players then add up to its goal difference with R² 0.890 over 1170 team-seasons 2014-2026 (GAR on the same seasons 0.879).

Replacement is the xG part of the bottom-three sides' regulars, less sides that collapsed (GK -0.123, D -0.075, M -0.036, F -0.004 a 90), with finishing and saves at league average. League strength is ×0.058 a goal of club rating.
Weights fit on the same season (team goal difference, or first half to second half) could not split a side's xG between its players. The team totals are the same either way, so GAR's split is kept.
entries.where: soccer SVAR leaders, rookies, all-time players, transactions; conviction awards (Ballon d'Or pool by SVAR)

entries.short: The stand-in for soccer GAR and SVAR in a league where Understat is behind the results.
body: GAR is built on Understat's on-pitch data. When its match files trail a league by a round, that league's rows move to FotMob's season lists, and move back when Understat is in step.

A ridge fit per position maps FotMob's rates a 90 (npxG, xA, finishing, chances created, shots, passing, defensive actions, match rating, keepers' goals prevented) and the side's xG for and against to the player's Understat value a 90. The GAR fit also reads his Understat value from the season before. Held out by season 2020-2026, r is 0.93 for GAR and 0.95 for SV.

Rate = w × the frozen Understat rate + (1 - w) × the FotMob estimate, and the total is the rate × FotMob's minutes. w = a × min / (min + k) on his frozen minutes. With three quarters of the matches seen, a is 0.8 for GAR and 0.6 for SV. With a quarter seen, 0.4 and 0.4. A player Understat never saw gets the FotMob estimate.

Test: Understat frozen at a quarter, half and three quarters of each season, scored on the full-season totals of 14,342 player-seasons. Frozen at three quarters, RMSE of SVAR is 0.70 for the frozen total, 0.49 for the frozen rate on current minutes and 0.40 for the blend (t -20.9, 6 of 6 seasons). GAR: 0.67, 0.43, 0.39 (t -18.4).
Frozen at a quarter, SVAR RMSE goes from 1.66 to 0.53, and the top 150's rank correlation with the final order from 0.40 to 0.85.
Blended into GAR while Understat is up, it adds nothing to next season (team R² 0.569 against 0.568, t 0.7), so it is only the fallback.
entries.where: Soccer SVAR leaders, rookies, awards, xMV and projections in a league Understat trails

entries.short: Kick and punt return yards over expected, shrunk.
body: YOE is return yards minus the mean return from the same spot (5-yard bins, this season). It uses yards instead of EPA, since EPA doesn't repeat.
entries.where: special teams tab on NFL and CFB pages

entries.short: The outcome per recruit over what his recruiting rating predicted, shrunk by sample.
body: CFB: NFL FV per signee, with a school tau of .42 FV, rolling t = 5.3 (6/6). CBB NBA FV is null, and the college BPM change passes.
CBB head coach BPM over expected: split t = 5.1. Shown with +/- 1 SD.
entries.where: development tab on CFB and CBB pages

entries.short: P(declares) × P(picked in the 2027 draft).
body: Declare is a logit on ln xPick and age on draft day. Ranked underclassmen declare about 94% of the time, seniors about 69% and RS seniors 100%.
Picked is a log-normal around the mock xPick, with an SD that narrows toward the draft (PFF dated boards, 2020-26).

entries.short: The chance a player is back in college next season instead of in the 2027 draft, 1 - P(declares).
body: CFB uses the Draft% declare logit (ln xPick, age on draft day, by class group). Leaving one draft out on the 2021-25 fall PFF boards (564 prospects, without RS seniors and grads), log loss is 0.313, compared to 0.411 for class only, 0.416 for class + position and 0.456 for the base rate (t = -5.5, 9/10 draft × class cells).

A reported return in the decision window (CFB Nov 20 to the January deadline, CBB Mar 15 to the withdrawal date) sets Ret% to 97% in both sports. In CFB there were 18 reported returners in the 2023-2025 drafts, and 0% declared (the model said 46%). Log loss goes from 1.01 to 0.05, t = -3.9, 3/3 cycles. A reported declaration failed (t = -1.2).

CBB uses class, era (NIL 2022+, COVID 2021, the 2024+ step), recruit rank and BPM shrunk by minutes. Walk-forward 2023-26, log loss is 0.284, compared to 0.329 for class and era (t = -4.7). The 2024+ step is t = -4.0, 4/4. With the midseason board on top, leaving one draft out 2022-26, board-listed players are 0.495 compared to 0.641 for the base rate.
CBB reported return: 69 players, 0% left (the model said 20%), t = -4.6, 3/3. It passed.

Failed on top of the live model in both sports (each one was tried in both): PFF grade x snaps (CFB; the BPM analogue), recruit rank (CFB), height, COVID year (CFB), NIL 2022+ step (CFB), NIL x xPick, NIL x age, rookie deal vs NIL, QB, Power 4 / high-major, age in class (CBB), age (CBB), guard (QB analogue), NIL x BPM, NIL x recruit rank.

Draft pay in dollars (first-year cash over the pick spread against college pay, each scaled to its year's salary cap and NIL market) failed in CFB (t = 1.9 as a log ratio, 2.1 as a dollar gap, 2022-25 boards). In CBB the dollar gap passes leaving one draft out (t = -3.2, 5/5), but it is the year level and not the player: beside a 2024+ step it is t = -0.5, and walking forward t = -1.9. It didn't ship. Board ranks 31-60: 62% left in 2022-23 (n = 47) and 22% in 2025-26 (n = 37; the model said 45%).
entries.where: CFB draft board, CBB draft board

entries.short: The chance a player is on another FBS or FCS roster next season.
body: A ridge logit on the 2024-25 and 2025-26 cycles: class, production, role, recruit rank, record, P(HC change) and distance from home.
Out-of-time AUC is .738. Transfer% + stay + exit = 100%. It uses NIL-era data only (July 2021 on).
Coach ties: in CBB the head coach's seasons at the school lower it (2025-26 held out t = 2.89, log loss 0.8831, AUC 0.727); in CFB the same term failed (t = -2.25).

A transfer who came with his head coach moved again 16.9% of the time in CBB against 20.8% for other transfers (n = 124), and 14.4% against 14.9% in CFB (n = 194). Too few to pass held out (t = -0.91 CBB, 0.98 CFB). Seasons under the coach, players he inherited and a coach leaving x the tie failed in both sports too.
entries.where: CFB board, portal, team builder; CBB portal

entries.short: Two terms for the miles from a player's hometown to each school: log distance, and inside 150 miles.
body: The hometown comes from the recruiting history (ranked recruits, 27% of moves). With no hometown on file, both terms are 0 for every school.
Fit on 2022-24 moves and held on 2025-26 moves with a hometown (n 371),
log loss of the chosen school goes from 5.395 to 5.244 (t = 4.56 by origin team), and the top-10 hit rate from 12.1% to 21.8%. On all moves, top-10 goes from 12.6% to 15.1%.
A school within 150 miles of home has a coefficient of +.52, and log miles -.35.

entries.short: The chance an FCS player is on an FBS roster next season.
body: A logit on 2023-26 FCS-to-FBS moves: production, team strength, year in school and position. It is capped at 1 - Draft%.

entries.short: The chance a D-II or D-III player is on a D-I roster next season.
body: A ridge logit on NCAA D-II/III box scores, for the 2023-24 and 2024-25 move-ups: production, starts, minutes, team SRS and division.
Out of time on 2025-26 to 2026-27, AUC is .899 and log loss is .077, compared to .111 for the base rate.
FV = 20 + D-1% × V. V is his line translated to a first D-I season (shrunk BPM; a ridge on 318 movers, out of time r .43/.60),
then what the 2009-16 arrivals with that season and class became (Poisson index + monotone map, out-of-fold deviance t = 2.8).

entries.short: The chance a college player leaves school for this NBA draft.
body: Recruit rank, minutes-shrunk BPM, class and era, plus the midseason board rank. Seniors and internationals are 100%.

entries.short: The 20th, 50th and 80th percentile of WAR, VORX and stats, for the full season and the rest of the season.
body: Rest of season = rate × exposure (minutes, TOI, snaps), where the rate is a Marcel 1 / .7 / .5 with a fitted shrink.
It is recalibrated for each season-left bin, and checked by PIT on held-out seasons (+/- .03 overall).
entries.where: projections tab on NFL, NBA, NHL pages

entries.short: The chance of each award, from a voter model on simulated rests of the season, blended with Polymarket where a liquid market is open.
body: The model is 3,000 simulated rests of the season, with each finish scored by a voter model fit on past ballots.
The blend is model^.05 × market^.95, renormalised. On 7 held 2025-26 races, winner log loss was 2.32 for the model, 1.12 for the market and 1.13 for the blend (t = -2.3).
It is blended only when the event has 3+ two-sided quotes, prices summing within 25% of 1 and $50,000 traded. Otherwise it is the model only.
The cell hover keeps the model number, and the weekly ledger scores the model alone against the market.
Conviction view: P(lead) is the share of simulations in which he leads the award's pool on this season's value alone.
The games left run at this season's own rate, with no last season, no shrunk or predictive rate, no voter model and no market.
NFL and CFB use SVAR by position (no SV for OL, K, P or CFB defence). NBA uses VORX, and D-XPM for DPOY. NHL uses WAR, and GSAx for the Vezina. CBB uses BPM.
Soccer uses SVAR (GAR rebuilt from this season alone: a one-season xG plus-minus, with finishing and keeper saves at face value).
entries.where: Awards tabs (predictive awards, conviction awards): NBA, NFL, NHL, CFB, CBB, soccer

entries.short: 3Y WAR is the chance he plays in the next three seasons × his WAR if he does.
body: The stay chance is a logistic on pWAR pace, age, age squared, ln TOI per 82 and the share of team games played.
WAR if he plays is the 3Y form refit on the players who stayed.
Leaving one season out 2010-23, skaters RMSE goes from 2.455 to 2.447 (t = -6.9 by season, 14 of 14) and goalies from 4.074 to 4.066 (t = -3.0, 10 of 14).
It is kept at every season share from .1 to 1.
The IN 3Y column (skaters) is the chance he plays in season S+3. Its held-out error is under 3 points in every tenth.
Goalies fail that check (up to 10 points), so they get no column.
NBA: 3Y XPM = stay × XPM given he plays + (1 - stay) × -2. The numbers are under 1Y / 3Y XPM.
entries.where: NHL value board (3Y, IN 3Y); NBA VORX/XPM leaders (3Y)

entries.short: Per-game points, rebounds and assists (NBA, CBB) and fantasy lines (NFL, CFB).
body: The NBA version walks the game model's minutes and P(play), plus pace, opponent and the minutes freed up by teammates who are out.
Held out 2024-26, PRA MAE is 6.20, compared to 6.46 for the season average. CBB is 5.42 compared to 5.58.
NBA minutes in a team's first 10 games add preseason starts (the share of the last two preseason games started,
fading to 0 by game 11). In games 1-10, held 2024-26, minutes MAE goes from 4.714 to 4.676 (t = -3.48, 3/3 seasons).

entries.short: A player's projection minus the replacement projection at his position, in a 12-team league.
body: Replacement is the first non-starter: QB13, RB30, WR31, TE13, K13, DST13. The overall rank is by VOR.

entries.short: Young players' weekly WAR over expected.
body: xWAR = his WAR rate a snap before the week (three seasons shrunk to the group, updated in season) × snaps.

entries.short: First and second-year QB, RB, WR and TE whose touches and targets are rising.
body: It lists usage growth. It is a watch list, and no model grade is behind it.

entries.short: The chance of a first season at a quality bar next season, for players who have never reached it.
body: The bar is a shrunk value near the 75-80th percentile of regulars. Anyone already over it (career, this season included) is out.
NBA: BPM +1.0, 1,000+ MP. CBB: BPM +2.8, 40%+ min. NHL: WAR/1,000 min 1.19. Soccer: GAR/90 .090. NFL: PPR/G 12 (TE 9). CFB: PFN z .32.
A logistic on shrunk value plus signals. Each signal is added alone, leaving one season out, and needs t >= 2 and most seasons won, then Holm.
The age or class curve passes everywhere. Low-volume efficiency and the projection gap pass in most sports. CBB adds team context (t = 3.8) and the pXPM gap.
Failed: vacated role (all six sports), coaching change, opportunity ahead, improvement trend, splines, Platt, and boosted trees (they never beat the logistic).
Held-out t: NBA 7.9, CBB 14.4, NHL 5.6, soccer 6.2, CFB 6.0, NFL 3.3.
entries.where: next up tab on every sport page

entries.short: A player's projected output at a bigger workload, from players whose workload changed.
body: Workload is USG (NBA, CBB), TOI split EV/PP (NHL), shot involvement SI% (soccer) and target or touch share (NFL).
Next-season efficiency on this season's, shrunk for sample, plus workload change × context blocks, in a ridge held out by season.
A workload change alone doesn't drop efficiency on average, which is selection: players earn the work.
NBA: the shot profile sets the slope (high-2P% finishers lose the most). CBB: shot profile, role, frame, level and low-usage rates.
NHL: EV P/60 rises with minutes (instrumented, 0.14 a minute). Soccer: role. NFL RB: -0.23 Y/OPP per 10 share points.
Tiers past the 99th percentile of observed jumps are beyond the data. CFB has no tiers, since every test failed.
CEIL is an 80th percentile season one tier up (NBA/CBB usage +5, NHL TOI +3, soccer SI% +10), on role seasons: mean + q × spread.
CEIL scales: NBA XPM, CBB BPM, NHL shrunk WAR/1k, soccer shrunk GAR/90. Workload change × context passes in all four.
CEIL held-out t (pinball .80): NBA 3.9, CBB 6.1, NHL 6.0, soccer 9.3. Coverage is 79-80% of workload-up seasons.

entries.short: Second and third-string players who grade above a starter.
body: Gap = backup value - starter value (WAA and BPM with pXPM in college; WAR, pXPM, HPM or GAR in the pros).
They are ranked by xGap, the gap projected over two seasons with the age (or class) gap added. Held out t = -3.0 to -15.6.
NFL xGap projects from the pXP/60 gap on its own fit of 2,457 pairs: held out squared error .0429 to .0375, t 5.1, 5 of 5.
NHL adds the Marcel GAR a 60 gap (t -2.4, 9 of 10) and soccer the p/90 gap (t -5.9, 7 of 7) beside the grade gap.
NBA grades are pXPM: next season XPM error 1.301 to 1.185, t 13, 15 of 15. With pXPM already aged, its age term drops out.
entries.where: backup watch tab on every sport page

entries.short: The nearest historical profiles, shown in the player dropdown.
body: CFB uses the nearest 2014-22 profiles. Hockey stage 3-4 comps also feed FV (they passed held out). Everywhere else they are display only.

entries.short: A G League player's chance of NBA minutes next season, his chance of 500+ NBA minutes (per 82 games), and his expected NBA VORX over the next 3 seasons.
body: A ridge logistic (L2 1) on 8,036 G League seasons 2008-25, regular season + Showcase Cup, 50+ minutes. Showcase-only seasons 2022-25 are pooled in with a part-season flag.

Inputs: age, age^2, log minutes, games, the per-36 box (pts reb ast stl blk tov 3PA FTA, Game Score, +/-), TS%, usage, AST%, OREB%, DREB%, net rating and PIE; NBA minutes and XPM (shrunk to -2 with 500 MP) through last season; draft round, log pick and years since the draft.
xVORX = P(any NBA game in 3 seasons) × ridge E[3-season VORX | plays].

Leaving one season out, against the same model without G League stats: NBA% log loss is .338 compared to .378 (t = -6.2, 16/18 seasons) and AUC .883 compared to .846 (.912 and .872 for players with no NBA minutes yet). 500% is .191 compared to .207 (t = -4.3), AUC .897 compared to .862. xVORX RMSE is .921 compared to .981 (t = -3.1). All of them pass Holm.
It is calibrated by decile held out (the top NBA% decile was .87 predicted and .86 observed). The base rates are 23% / 8%.
A two-way to standard contract isn't modelled, since there is no contract-type history.
xXPM = ridge E[NBA XPM over his NBA minutes, next 3 seasons | plays], weighted by those minutes (lambda 300).
xVORX counts 0 for a season out of the NBA (75% of G League seasons), so it sits near 0 for most players. xXPM is the rate alone.
Held out against no G League stats, xXPM minute-weighted RMSE is 1.44 compared to 1.60 (t = -3.6, 11/15 seasons, Holm), with a bias of .01.

entries.short: The predictive SV rate, from this season and the two before.
body: SV a 90 at weights 1, .5, .25, shrunk toward the position mean of regulars by 225 minutes (defenders 450, keepers 28,800),
minus .008 a year over age 29. Held out, next-season team GD R² goes from .634 to .650, 11 of 11 pairs,
and r with next season's SV a 90 from .690 to .718. It is the most predictive soccer metric on players.
1Y / 3Y count the two seasons before twice over, as GAR and as SVAR, pooled a 90 and shrunk with 900 minutes.
With SVAR in, the GAR prior's weight falls to about zero. Held out 1Y RMSE 1.310 to 1.305, t -2.6 (Nov 27 2026).
entries.where: Soccer SVAR leaders, depth chart, next up, backup watch xGap

entries.term: Most predictive and most descriptive metric (by sport)
entries.short: Each sport's metrics scored on one test, held out, with no 2026-27 outcomes.
body: Describe: season value × season minutes summed for each team, on that season's results, held out. Predict: season n value ×
season n+1 minutes, on n+1 results, and a player's value against his next season. Tennis and CS2 use held-out matches and maps.
NBA: describe rXPM (.999), predict pXPM (.657). NFL: describe XV (.604), predict pXP/60 within position, AV for teams (.317).
CFB: describe XV (.689), predict cWAR (.256, tie XV). CBB: describe VORX on rXPM, predict pXPM in board form.
NHL: describe WAR (.978), predict pWAR for teams (.387), Marcel WAR for a player (r .446). Soccer: describe SVAR (.894),
predict p/90 (.650, r .718). Tennis: describe PA (.141), predict ARK (.107, tie Elo). CS2: describe season RWA, predict RWA rating
(next month team R² .124, player r .820), ARK for teams. The public metrics scored were nflverse EPA, PFN impact, Barttorvik PRPG,
MoneyPuck game score, FotMob rating, Transfermarkt value, official tennis rank, an HLTV 2.0 style rating and the bo3.gg rating. None of them leads.
entries.where: Every ARKBOARD: descriptive tabs lead with the describe pick, predictive tabs with the predict pick

entries.short: The chance an uncommitted recruit signs with each school on his recruitment list. The top school is shown in the Team cell.
body: A conditional logit over his ESPN recruitment list (3+ schools), fit walk-forward by class, with a recency weight of .75 a class (CFB).
Terms: program pull and tier, grade × tier, hometown distance, home state, conversion rate (signed / listed) and on-field Elo (CFB).

CFB also uses On3/Rivals visits (official, unofficial count, latest, last 90 days) and the confidence-weighted share of On3 expert picks. It is trained as of 30 days before each commitment, and live it uses everything to date.

Held out 2018-26 (CFB), log loss goes from 1.962 to 1.896 and top-1 from 30.4% to 32.3%. RPM % on top of the picks failed (CFB), and so did every On3 term (CBB). Leans above 80% have run about 10-20 points hot.

Coach terms (CFB, classes 2022-26 held out): a school whose head coach is gone after the recruit's senior fall is picked less (t = 6.8, log loss 1.927 to 1.924). Head coach tenure passed alone (t = 3.9) but not in every class on top of that. Failed: a first-year coach (t = 1.5), a coach who came from a school on his list (t = 1.1), and all four in CBB (t = -1.2 to 0.6).
entries.where: CFB and CBB recruit class tabs

entries.short: Each sport's power ranking, which is the game model's neutral-site rating put in order.
body: It is the same number the game model uses, so the picks already read it. It splits into parts (Elo, efficiency, talent ...).
The rank range is the 80% range of the true rank, from 4,000 draws at the rating sd measured on past seasons.
In CBB 2016-26, ARK picks the winner 77.3% of the time compared to 76.8% for the AP poll, and 77.1% compared to 76.7% for the Coaches poll.
entries.where: ARK Ranking tab on every sport page; ARKRANKING page

entries.short: Points against an average FBS team on a neutral field.
body: Elo (with a preseason prior from last season, SP+, 247 talent, returning production and transfers) + opponent-adjusted EPA/play.
Plus home, rest, travel, altitude, FCS (and the FCS side's own margin rating), special teams, P4 tier, 4th-down aggressiveness, returning production
and game control. The sim's win sd is 14.2. Current injuries are charged (Inj), and Full is the team at full strength.
entries.where: CFB ARK Ranking, games, season odds

entries.short: Expected margin against an average team on a neutral field, with this week's QB and injuries.
body: Fitted terms: Elo, starting QB, rest, home, injuries, a market rating from earlier closes, and the return game.
Injury cost = WAR a game × 36 points a win × P(miss), where questionable is .25 and doubtful is .98.
entries.where: NFL ARK Ranking, games, season odds

entries.short: Expected margin against an average D-I team on a neutral floor.
body: Fitted terms: adjusted efficiency × possessions, Elo, home, game control, conference home game, injuries,
home × attendance, ESPN BPI, form and the preseason injury report. The preseason prior comes from returning minutes, transfers and top-5 FV.
50% of three-point luck is taken out.

Market disagreement is each team's running gap between its earlier closes and the model (.2 a game, 0 at the start of the season), for spreads and totals. On lined games 2021-26, margin MAE goes from 9.057 to 9.009 (the close is 8.986) and totals from 13.401 to 13.366.
entries.where: CBB ARK Ranking, games, season odds, tournament odds

entries.short: Expected margin against an average team on a neutral floor, with the current roster and today's injury report.
body: Fitted terms: Elo, net rating, market rating, home, lineup value (XPM × minutes × chance to play), playoff Elo and rest.
25% of three-point luck is taken out. The Proj column (rest-of-season VORX) is display only.
entries.where: NBA ARK Ranking, games, season odds

entries.short: Win chance from a logistic on Elo, an expected-goals rating, back-to-backs, home and lineup value.
body: The xG rating is an opponent-adjusted ridge with a half-life of 120 days, and .7 of it carries over a season. Lineup value follows trades.
Totals use xG, goals, the market total and the starting goalie.
entries.where: NHL ARK Ranking, games, season odds

entries.short: Goals a match against an average big-five club on neutral ground, on one scale for every league.
body: An online Poisson attack and defence rating within each league, with league strength from cross-league matches only.
The inputs are blended walk-forward: market-implied goals from earlier closes, xG (Understat, FotMob) and squad value.
Dixon-Coles rho is -.04. In the big five, held out, log loss is .972 compared to .967 for the close.
entries.where: Soccer ARK Ranking, league tabs, UEFA cups, MLS

entries.short: League goal difference a match above the game model's pre-match expectation, by manager.
body: Residual = the actual 90-minute GD minus the walk-forward model's expected GD, shrunk with 40 average matches,
for managers with 100+ matches, 2012-13 to 2025-26 (Transfermarkt managers).
As a term in a manager's first 10 matches at a new club it failed (held 2023-26 t = -0.05).

entries.short: Win chance against the average top-50 player in a best of three, over the tour's 52-week surface mix.
body: Surface Elo blended with a games-won rating and opponent-adjusted serve and return point ratings (Markov chain).
It is fit on 2012-22 tour main draws. Held 2023-26, log loss is about .596, compared to .603 for Elo.
SV is season WAR for the calendar year to date, at every level, with the same credit per match as WAR.
Split-half r is .81 ATP and .82 WTA (2015 to 2025), and next-season r is .85 ATP and .84 WTA.
ARK adds the points added term, CP × pPA gap / 10 on the match blend. Next-season log loss t = -8.7, 14 of 15 seasons.
rPA is shrunk by 300 points toward 0, which moves held-out describe R² from .128 to .135 (15 of 15). WAR counts Futures and ITF at half,
and Challenger, qualifying and team events at .85 (next-season R² .083 to .085, t = -7.1). SV keeps every match in full.

entries.short: Series win chance against the average top-20 team.
body: A player Elo that follows players between rosters (per map, on round share), the bo3.gg team map rating with veto,
region offsets, Valve VRS points and the five players' mean RWA. Held out log loss is .553, compared to .667 for VRS. There are no picks, since there is no free closing odds history.
Valve lists one series up to several times under alias team names (9,624 of 37,399 rows). Repeats of a date and
both fives are dropped before every replay. Held log loss on the clean rows: ARK .6105, team RWA .6245, VRS .6640.

entries.short: A rating from results and margin, where 1500 is average.
body: CFB Elo starts from a preseason prior. In CS2 Elo, +400 is 10 to 1 odds. Tennis Elo is on wins, at every level.

entries.short: How much of each game a team spent with the win in hand.
body: A time-weighted win chance from score and clock only, opponent-adjusted and carried across seasons.
It shipped in CFB (held out MAE t = -4.1) and CBB (t = -2.0). It failed in the NBA.

entries.short: Talent is the value of the projected starters by FV, and TvE is Elo against the Elo that talent predicts, in SD.
body: CFB Talent is the sum over the projected starting 22 of expected college WAR a season at FV. A TvE above 0 means the team is playing above its talent.

entries.short: 10,000 simulated seasons from the game model.
body: The rating error sd shrinks with the season left (sd^2 = a + b × share left, measured on past seasons).
xW = wins so far + the simulated rest. The outputs are conference, playoff and title odds, with full NFL tiebreakers.
In the NHL I tested the preseason points over/under as the sim's prior, and it isn't used.
In 2014-19 there was no gain at any weight (points MAE +.01, t = +.1). In 2020-26 it was -.21 points (t = -8.8, 7/7 seasons), and playoff Brier went from .1635 to .1591.
